candidates.title: LLM Agents Can Easily Tamper With Their Own Traces
candidates.institution: ELLIS Institute Tuebingen + Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems + Snyk
communitySignals: project page perfect-crime.ai with interactive figures
not on HF Daily Papers (weekend announcement)
credibilityEvidence: Section 3.1 Figure 2: ASR across 10 model-harness pairs x 4 direct-request scenarios, 10 trials each
Section 3.1 Figure 3: full-access vs auto-mode permission ablation
Section 3.2 Figure 6: skill-injection exploitability experiment without user knowledge
Section 3.3 Figure 7: reward-optimization misalignment-propensity experiment, 2 tasks x 10 trials
Section 3.4 Figure 8: multi-agent peer-cascade experiment (Peer Logs / Peer Workspaces)
Section 4 proposes and specifies an independent-interception-server mitigation architecture
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Covers capability, exploitability, misalignment propensity, peer cascade and aftereffects with quantified ASR per scenario and qualitative trace case studies; does not cover provider-side telemetry or whether tool calls are faithfully executed
reproducibilityEvidence: project page perfect-crime.ai publishes interactive charts and per-experiment quantitative results; no code or raw dataset repository found
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Multi-scenario, multi-model quantified ASR plus qualitative case studies support the scoped claim that current mainstream harnesses cannot prevent agents from tampering with their own traces
candidates.primaryLimitation: Study scoped to client-side logging pipeline only, excluding provider-side records and independent telemetry; proposed mitigation only guarantees post-API trace integrity, not faithful tool execution
candidates.presentationReason: Method, threat model, experimental setup and limitations are laid out precisely with explicit figures and per-scenario ASR tables
candidates.reason: Selected: breaks the foundational assumption of post-hoc agent audit/compliance/forensics; first systematic 10-harness test with reward-optimization and peer-cascade propensity results going beyond prior single-scenario red-teaming work
